newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency said sticking to air bag stance.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency said sticking to air bag stance.

text.p: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is sticking to its original proposal to allow broad, on-demand deactivation of air bags, the Washington Post reported in Tuesday editions.

A draft rule now being reviewed by the Office of Management and Budget would give motorists the choice of an on-off switch or mechanical disconnection of the air bags, the paper said, quoting government and industry sources.

The draft proposal could be announced as a final rule by the end of June, but only after the NHTSA and the White House resolve a dispute over when motorists should be allowed to turn off their air bags, the sources told the Post.
Automakers and insurers have strongly resisted the proposal, arguing that giving consumers broad ability to deactivate air bags would essentially make the mandatory safety feature an option.

Air bags have been credited with saving 1,900 lives since 1986, but they have also been blamed for the deaths of 40 children and 27 adults since 1990, primarily because of the rapid speed and extreme force with which they deploy in even minor accidents.
